stories.headline: Anthropic Embeds D&B, Verisk, Moody's and Other Data Giants Directly Into Claude for Financial Services
stories.summary: Anthropic's expanded Claude for Financial Services platform now includes native connectors to Dun & Bradstreet, Verisk, Experian, Moody's, LSEG, S&P Capital IQ, and others — letting financial analysts query these data sources without leaving the Claude interface. Moody's gets the marquee billing as a native app for credit ratings on 600M+ companies, but D&B's inclusion confirms the 'be everywhere' strategy is paying off in practice. This is the Visa analogy made real: D&B data flowing inside third-party AI workflows rather than requiring customers to come to D&B directly.

stories.headline: Forrester: 75% of Enterprises Claim Agentic AI Adoption, But Scaled Multiagent Deployments Remain Rare
stories.summary: Forrester's new 'State of Agentic AI, 2026' report finds three-quarters of enterprise leaders say they are adopting agentic AI, yet only a small minority have it running in meaningful production beyond basic chatbots — with true scaled multiagent systems rarer still. The report frames 2026 as the year the technology outpaced enterprise readiness, with governance, data quality, and integration gaps as the primary blockers. For D&B, the governance and data-foundation gap is a direct opening: agents that can't trust their underlying data are agents that fail, which is precisely the 'Ground Truth' positioning D&B owns.

stories.headline: Walnut Launches Family of AI Agents to Personalize the B2B Buyer Experience at Scale
stories.summary: Walnut, used by hundreds of B2B software go-to-market teams, launched AI Mode for Playlists and Deal Rooms alongside 'Walnut Xpert' — an agent that lets buyers self-navigate product demos via natural language. The announcement (September 2, 2026) signals that agentic AI is now penetrating the buyer-side of the B2B sales motion, not just the seller side. This matters for D&B's Prospecting and Account Intelligence agent archetypes: as buyers complete 60-70% of research before speaking to a rep, agents need richer, more timely account intelligence to intercept buying windows earlier.

stories.headline: Deloitte and NVIDIA Data: Only 1 in 5 Enterprises Has a Mature Governance Model for Agentic AI
stories.summary: Deloitte's 2026 State of AI in the Enterprise report finds that while 23% of companies now report at least moderate use of agentic AI, only one in five has a mature governance framework for autonomous agents — a gap NVIDIA's own surveys corroborate as companies shift from static AI tools to systems that take sequential actions autonomously. The governance deficit is not a compliance abstraction: it directly affects financial processes, customer interactions, and logistics chains. D&B's explainability-first positioning — providing auditable, sourced ground truth to agentic decisions — is a direct answer to what CFOs and risk teams are demanding before they scale.

stories.headline: Private Credit Stress Concentrated in 2021-2022 Vintages as AI Disruption Compounds Software Sector Defaults
stories.summary: Valuation Research Corp's Q2 2026 Private Markets update finds credit dispersion widening, with stress concentrated in 2021-2022 vintage loans and software-related exposures — where higher borrowing costs, weaker fundamentals, and AI-related disruption are driving increased restructurings. Fitch Ratings is forecasting institutional loan default rates in the 4.5-5.0% range, while software direct lending now prices at 75-100 basis points above year-end levels. For D&B, rising commercial credit stress — particularly in tech-sector borrowers — validates the strategic value of real-time Paydex and financial risk signals, and makes the Pipeline Risk & Revenue Protection agent archetype increasingly urgent for customers with software-heavy account portfolios.

stories.headline: Labs Race to Gate Cyber AI Capabilities — Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI All Ship 'Defender' Model Tiers in September
stories.summary: In the first ten days of September, Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI each released new frontier models — Claude Fable 5.1/Mythos 5.1, Gemini 3.8 Flash, and GPT-6 Astra — and all three simultaneously introduced gated 'cyber' capability tiers available only to vetted security researchers and defenders. The defining pattern is a deliberate split between a model's raw intelligence and its permission to use that intelligence offensively, with access regimes diverging even as underlying capabilities converge across labs. For D&B, this signals that enterprise AI deployments will increasingly need to manage tiered model access policies — a compliance and governance layer where D&B's entity-resolution and explainability stack can add direct value.

stories.headline: OpenAI Opens Managed Agents API in Public Beta — Turns ChatGPT Work Infrastructure Into Developer Platform
stories.summary: On September 13, OpenAI launched a managed Agents API in public beta, handling orchestration, long-running sessions, and context management for autonomous agents, with sandbox compute available from OpenAI and partners including Vercel and DigitalOcean. The scaled-agent infrastructure previously powering ChatGPT Work is now a public API, with agent spin-up times under a minute. This is a direct move to lock developers into OpenAI's agentic stack — precisely the platform layer D&B must embed into to remain the neutral data layer of record across all agentic workflows, reinforcing the 'be everywhere' Visa analogy.

stories.headline: EU AI Act High-Risk Enforcement Goes Live — European AI Office Begins Formal Audits in September
stories.summary: The transition period for general high-risk AI systems under the EU AI Act concluded on August 2, 2026, and throughout September the European AI Office and national authorities are executing active statutory enforcement including audits, with new transparency rules now requiring chatbots to disclose AI identity and deepfakes to carry mandatory labels. Separately, on September 16, the Council of Europe's Framework Convention on AI — described as the first internationally legally binding instrument dedicated to AI governance — formally entered into force. Enterprises using AI in consequential decisions now face real enforcement risk, not just compliance preparation, making explainable and auditable data sources like D&B's scored attributes (Paydex, Buydex) a harder requirement rather than a differentiator.

stories.headline: Connecticut Passes Most Comprehensive US State AI Law of 2026 — Mandatory Transparency Obligations Now Live
stories.summary: Connecticut's SB 5 passed in the 2026 legislative session as the most far-reaching state AI statute of the year, creating a regulatory sandbox, chatbot disclosure controls, and ADS-style transparency requirements that compel developers to pass compliance-relevant system information to deployers, and deployers to disclose adverse AI-driven decisions to affected employees. With 85 new AI-related laws now enacted across 27 US states in 2026, and six states still in active session, the US patchwork is thickening rapidly even as federal preemption remains stalled. For D&B, state-level mandates for documented, auditable AI decision inputs will drive enterprise buyers toward vendors whose data provenance and scoring methodology can withstand regulatory scrutiny.
stories.source: Transparency Coalition / Center for Democracy and Technology

stories.headline: Farage Hits Record-Low Approval as Labour and Reform Draw Level at 23% Each
stories.summary: The latest YouGov tracker shows Nigel Farage's net favourability has fallen to -45 — his worst-ever reading in a decade of polling — after Reform's annual conference was dogged by fresh donation allegations. Labour and Reform are now statistically tied at 23% of voting intention apiece, with the Conservatives on 20% and the Greens surging to 11–12%, reflecting what analysts describe as an unprecedented fragmentation of British political allegiances. The figures are a stark reminder that no single party commands broad public confidence heading into the pre-election period.

stories.headline: Trump Campaigns in North Carolina as Midterm Fever Builds — ICE Nominee Withdrawn
stories.summary: President Trump held a rally in Gastonia, North Carolina on 16 September as his administration ramps up midterm campaign activity, while the White House simultaneously withdrew the nomination of Lance Schroyer — a former Oklahoma state trooper — to lead ICE, amid scrutiny of the agency's enforcement record. Separate lawsuits filed this week allege that repeated Trump administration suggestions about placing federal officers at polling sites constitute illegal voter intimidation, a charge the administration disputes. The flurry of political and legal activity signals an increasingly charged atmosphere ahead of November's midterm elections.

stories.headline: NASA's Roman Space Telescope Could Run for 22+ Years — More Than Double Its Design Life
stories.summary: An exceptionally precise course-correction manoeuvre has left NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope with enough fuel for at least 22 years of science operations, compared to its original 10-year design life. The telescope, set to transform surveys of dark energy and exoplanets, now represents a significant extension of the agency's deep-space observational capability. The news comes as NASA navigates other delays, including a postponed Crew-13 Dragon launch after an oxidiser leak was discovered during pre-launch preparations.

stories.headline: BMW PGA Championship: Ryan Gerard Leads at Halfway as McIlroy Lurks Four Back at Wentworth
stories.summary: After 36 holes at Wentworth, American Ryan Gerard holds a two-shot lead at the halfway stage of the BMW PGA Championship, with Rory McIlroy — bidding for his second title at the Surrey course — lying four shots off the pace after a solid opening 69. Jon Rahm endured a nightmare, reportedly carding one of the highest scores seen on the DP World Tour this season and facing the cut. Round 3 is underway today (Saturday), with final-round coverage scheduled for Sunday morning.

stories.headline: Brentford Thrash Chelsea 3–0 as Premier League's New Boys Continue to Impress
stories.summary: Brentford produced a commanding performance to beat Chelsea 3–0 on Thursday 17 September in the 2026–27 Premier League, piling pressure on a Chelsea side that has now struggled for consistency early in the campaign. The result continues to underline the competitive depth of this season's top flight, which features newly promoted Sunderland, Hull City and Leeds United all holding their own. A further round of matches — including Manchester City vs Sunderland and Bournemouth vs Liverpool — is scheduled for today, Saturday 19 September.

stories.headline: Premiership Rugby's Franchise Era One Week Away — Ten Clubs, No Relegation, New Era Begins
stories.summary: With the 2026–27 Gallagher Premiership season kicking off on 25 September, English rugby union is days away from its most structurally significant change in decades: automatic promotion and relegation has been abolished in favour of a closed, franchise-based ten-club model. The new format is designed to give clubs financial stability and encourage greater investment, though it has divided fan opinion sharply. Northampton Saints enter as reigning champions, and all eyes will be on whether the franchise model delivers the competitive and commercial uplift its backers promise.

stories.headline: CERN Physicists Find Evidence of One of the Higgs Boson's Rarest Decays
stories.summary: Scientists at CERN have announced evidence for one of the rarest decay modes of the Higgs boson, a landmark result that probes the fundamental structure of the Standard Model of particle physics. The finding, published on 16 September, adds a new dimension to our understanding of how the particle that gives matter its mass actually behaves. Separately, CERN researchers also confirmed that quantum entanglement survives the violence of the Large Hadron Collider's high-energy collisions — a result with implications for quantum information science.

stories.headline: Some of All Fears: Ben Thompson on AI's Existential Reckoning and the Limits of Continuous Learning
stories.summary: Published September 18, 2026, Thompson's latest Stratechery article challenges the AGI declarations swirling after OpenAI's Astra release, arguing that true AGI requires continuous learning — a bar no current large language model meets. He grounds the critique in a concrete example: AI systems failing on real-world tasks because their knowledge cuts off at training time, making temporal freshness a structural weakness in today's deployed models. For D&B, this is a direct validation of the Temporal Analytics thesis — agents that lack continuously updated, trusted data signals (like Paydex payment trends or Buydex buying-window signals) will systematically mislead decision-makers. D&B's real-time data layer is precisely the patch for the gap Thompson identifies.

stories.headline: AI, Tools and Transformation: Why the People Who Need Automation Most Can't See It
stories.summary: Published September 3, 2026, Benedict Evans argues that AI faces a structural discovery problem: the professionals whose workflows most need automation — elite lawyers, enterprise salespeople — are too focused on their craft to identify what software could do for them. Templates and onboarding flows (including 'Claude for X' wrappers) paper over the gap rather than solving it, and every unfilled template slot represents a company waiting to be built. For D&B, this frames a critical go-to-market insight: embedding AI decision intelligence directly into the tools enterprise sales and risk teams already use (Salesforce Agentforce, Microsoft Copilot) removes the discovery burden entirely. The agent finds the workflow; the user doesn't have to.

stories.headline: 2026 State of AI Agents: Governance Is the New Deployment Bottleneck
stories.summary: Databricks' 2026 State of AI Agents report — drawing on data from over 20,000 global organizations including more than 60% of the Fortune 500 — finds that multi-agent systems grew 327% in under four months, and that companies using AI evaluation tools get nearly six times more projects into production. The report's sharpest finding: for organizations with AI governance frameworks in place, that production ratio jumps to over 12x, making governance the single highest-leverage investment in enterprise AI. For D&B, this reinforces the Explainability First pillar — enterprises deploying agentic AI need trusted, auditable ground truth at the data layer, not just model outputs. D&B's entity-resolved, temporally consistent business data is structurally what governance-conscious enterprises will reach for as they scale beyond pilots.

data_science.tagline: Teaching models to align with human judgment — the engine behind every useful LLM you've deployed.
data_science.what_it_is: RLHF is a training technique that fine-tunes a language or decision model using feedback signals derived from human preferences rather than fixed labels. Instead of telling a model 'the correct answer is X,' you show human raters pairs of outputs and ask which is better. Those preferences train a separate Reward Model, which then guides the main model via reinforcement learning (typically Proximate Policy Optimization, PPO) to produce outputs humans actually prefer. It's why ChatGPT gives structured, helpful responses instead of statistically likely but useless ones. RLHF sits at the intersection of supervised learning, reward modeling, and RL — and is the dominant technique behind aligning large language models (LLMs) to real-world task quality.
data_science.how_it_works: Step 1 — Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT): Start with a pretrained base LLM and fine-tune it on a curated dataset of high-quality prompt-response pairs. This gives the model a reasonable starting policy. Step 2 — Reward Model Training: Present human raters with multiple model outputs for the same prompt. Raters rank them by quality (accuracy, helpfulness, safety). These rankings become training data for a separate Reward Model (RM) — typically another LLM with a scalar output head — that learns to predict human preference scores for any given output. Step 3 — RL Fine-Tuning via PPO: The SFT model becomes the 'policy.' It generates outputs; the Reward Model scores them. PPO updates the policy to maximize reward scores while a KL-divergence penalty prevents the model from drifting too far from the original SFT baseline (avoiding reward hacking — gaming the RM with nonsensical but high-scoring outputs). Step 4 — Iteration: The cycle repeats with fresh human feedback on the updated model. A modern variant, Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), skips the explicit RM entirely and optimizes preferences directly into the policy, reducing complexity and instability. Key hyperparameters to control: KL penalty coefficient (β), PPO clip ratio, reward model capacity vs. policy capacity, and human rater consistency (inter-annotator agreement).
data_science.when_to_use: 1. You have a generative model producing outputs that are technically fluent but misaligned with business quality standards — e.g., hallucinated company names, wrong firmographic data, off-tone sales copy. 2. You cannot enumerate all correct answers with a labeled dataset but humans can reliably rank outputs. 3. You need to encode nuanced, subjective criteria (e.g., 'a good account summary is concise AND actionable') that resist simple loss functions. 4. You're deploying an LLM in a high-stakes workflow (credit risk commentary, compliance flags) where output tone and factual grounding matter enormously. Avoid RLHF when: your raters are inconsistent or low-quality (garbage reward model = garbage policy), your budget for human annotation is negligible, or a simpler prompt-engineering or DPO approach achieves the same alignment at lower cost.
data_science.worked_example: D&B's Sales Intelligence Copilot generates account summaries for sales reps — pulling from DUNS entity data, Paydex scores, corporate family trees, and news signals. The base LLM (fine-tuned on B2B content) produces summaries that are factually grounded but reps complain they're either too long, bury the key risk signal, or fail to highlight the right buying window trigger. RLHF fix: (1) SFT phase — fine-tune on 5,000 hand-curated 'gold standard' account briefs written by top sales analysts. (2) Reward Model — present 200 D&B sales reps with pairs of AI-generated summaries for 500 real accounts; reps pick the one they'd actually act on. Train a Reward Model on these 100,000 pairwise comparisons. The RM learns to score summaries higher when they: lead with a Paydex risk flag if score < 60, cite a specific buying signal (e.g., recent headcount growth in IT), keep total length under 120 words, and name the correct ultimate parent entity. (3) PPO loop — run 3 rounds of RL fine-tuning, each time generating new summaries, scoring with the RM, and updating the policy. KL penalty set high enough to prevent the model from learning to mention 'Paydex' robotically in every summary regardless of relevance. (4) Result — in a held-out evaluation, rep-preferred rate for AI summaries rises from 41% (SFT only) to 79% (post-RLHF). Pipeline coverage per rep increases 18% in the 90-day pilot because reps trust the output enough to act on it without manual verification. This is D&B's 'Explainability First' principle operationalized: the model doesn't just produce output — it produces output calibrated to what expert humans recognize as decision-ready intelligence.
resources: InstructGPT paper by Ouyang et al. (2022) — the foundational RLHF paper from OpenAI that introduced the SFT → RM → PPO pipeline for aligning LLMs
Anthropic's Constitutional AI paper (2022) — extends RLHF with AI-generated feedback (RLAIF), reducing human annotation burden while maintaining alignment quality
Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) paper by Rafailov et al. (2023, Stanford) — the practical modern alternative to PPO-based RLHF, simpler to implement and more stable to train
